questions.prompt: A curriculum run shows many more goal reaches in training than the fixed-start baseline, yet it fails from the true start at test time. What is the most likely cause?
options: Q-learning cannot be combined with any curriculum of starts
The goal reward was too large for the harder stages
The schedule never trained from the target start distribution
The learning rate was too high once the curriculum advanced
questions.explanation: Training hits measure the training distribution. If the target starts are never practised, their Q-values stay at their initial values.
questions.skillLabel: Check that the schedule ends on the target

questions.prompt: Symmetric random walk on cells 0..10, left at cell 0 stays, goal at cell 10. Expected steps from cell 0, T = (L - i)(L + i + 1)? (integer)
Budget 2000 split into 4 equal stages: which stage index (0-based) is active at t = 1500?
To compare a curriculum with a fixed-distribution baseline fairly you should give both
options: the same number of stages, with every stage given an equal share of the training time
the same number of episodes, whatever the length of each episode in environment steps
the same number of environment steps, seeds and evaluation on the target distribution
the same final training return, each measured on its own training start distribution
questions.explanation: Episode length differs between stages, so episodes are not an equal cost; training return is measured on different distributions.

questions.prompt: Reverse curriculum: budget 1500, 3 stages, corridor length 12, width 4. Start cell at t = 700 (max(0, length - width*(k+1)))? (integer)
Why does starting near the goal help a sparse-reward learner, and what quantity would you compute to check that stage 1 is easier?
rubric: Rewards are seen far more often under random exploration, giving a learning signal
Values then spread outward as the start moves back
Quantity: probability of reaching the goal within the episode cap (or expected steps) from the stage's start
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
